PILI, REB, REA Municipality of Bato, Province of Camarines Norte Dear Mr. Pili: This refers to your earlier letter wherein you are seeking this Department's legal opinion in relation to DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2019-86 with the subject "Strict Implementation of R.A. 9646 or the "Real Estate Service Act of the Philippines" According to your letter, the vacant position of Municipal Assessor in the later part of 2021, was occupied by Engr. Corazon A. Bonagua (Engr. Bonagua) on a permanent status. In addition, you alleged that Engr. Bonagua is an unlicensed real estate practitioner, which is a prohibition under Sec. 30 of Republic Act No. 9646 (R.A. 9646) otherwise known as the "Real Estate Service Act of the Philippines" Further, you emphasized DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2019-86 (MC No. 2019-86) re: "Strict Implementation of R.A. 9646 or the "Real Estate Service Act of the Philippines'% Under these premises arose your request for legal opinion on the following: I. Whether the appointment of Engr, Bonagua as Municipal Assessor is not affected by DILG MC No. 2019-86? 2. Is DILG MC No. 2019-86 still effective up to this date? 3. Whether Engr. Bonagua is entitled to receive monthly salary of P70, 728.00 plus allowances of P 14,000.00? 4. Whether Engr. Bonagua has not violated any of the provisions of R.A. 9646? 5. Is DILG MC No. 2019-86 being observed by the LGU? 6. Is the LGU strictly adhering to the provisions of R.A. 9646? At the outset, as to the 1st, 2nd 4th, 5th and 6th issue, considering that the issues are interrelated we deem it proper to address the same in one discussion. We would like to emphasize that R.A. 9646 was enacted to define what constitutes the official practice of real estate service in the Philippines. Accordingly, it is in furtherance of the policy of the State develop and nurture through a corps of technically competent, responsible and respected professional real estate service practitioners through proper and effective regulation and supervision. Correspondingly, we would like to emphasize that DILG MC No. 2019-86, is still effective, which was issued to reiterate pertinent provisions of R.A. 9646, and to establish baseline information on Professional Regulation Commission-licensed assessors in all local government units. Under Section 3.1.1.1 of the MC, all existinq and new positions in the national and local government. primarily requiring the services of any real estate practitioner. shall be filled b onl re istered and licensed real estate service ractitioners. Moreover, Section 3.1.2.1 reiterating Section 29 of R.A. 9646, states that: erson shall ractice or offer to ractice real estate service in the Phili ines or offer himself/herselfas real estate service ractitioner or use the title, word, letter, figure or any sign tending to convey the impression that one is a real estate service practitioner, or advertise or indicate in any manner whatsoever that one is qualified to practice the ptofession, or be appointed as real property appraiser or assessor in national government entity or local qovernment units, unless s/he has satisfactorily passed the licensure examination qiven by_ the Professional Requlatory Board, except as otherwise provided in R.A. 9646" Relatedly, Section 30 of R.A. 9646 states that "(w)ithin three (3) years from the effectivity of this Act, all existing and new positions in the national and local governments, whether career, permanent, temporary or contractual, and primarily requiring the services of any real estate service practitioner, shall be filled only by registered and licensed real estate service practitioners" In this regard, we are of the considered view that the act of the local government unit of appointing Engr. Bonagua as Municipal Assessor of the Municipality, despite being an unlicensed real estate practitioner, violates the provisions of R.A. 9646 and DILG MC No. 2019-86. In the same vein, Engr. Bonagua, in performing her duties as Municipal Assessor constitutes as practice of real estate, is also violative of the provisions of both R.A. 9646 and DILG MC No. 2019-86. As to the issue regarding entitlement to salary and allowances, we deem it appropriate to defer matter to the Civil Service Commission considering that it is the central personnel agency of the Government, having acquired "specialized knowledge and expertise" 1 in the field of civil service law. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly.
